title: Contextual recall nudge still overfires during procedural gap-store work
wanted_capability: Contextual-recall nudges should stay suppressed during procedural work that is already using the authoritative live state surface, such as bbox_gaps/bbox_gap checks for existing substrate gaps, unless a specific durable convention/decision/runbook could materially change the operation.
missing_primitive: runtime/rendered nudge suppression for procedural bbox_gaps/bbox_gap tasks after the prior contextual-recall overfire fix
fallback_used: Used bbox_gaps directly as the authoritative gap-store surface and ignored the repeated bbox_knowledge reminder as noise.
notes: Existing gap gap-5e3e3dff is marked addressed, but the current session reproduced the same operator-visible failure mode: while checking whether a bbox_knowledge over-nudging gap already existed, the agent used bbox_gaps as requested and still received repeated recall/reporting nudges. The operator explicitly challenged the noise ('why do you keep mentioning bbox_knowledge?') in the preceding task, making this a UX defect rather than just prompt-compliance chatter.
